title: La prime pour Luchini  (The Bonus for Luchini)

segments.t: New majority owner Hicham Janowski calls an impromptu meeting with the agents in his office. He criticizes the agency for relying on aging talent and urges them to recruit younger actors. To motivate the team, Hicham offers a generous bonus to anyone who keeps star actor Fabrice Luchini at ASK. Listen to the scene in French first. Don't worry about catching every word.
Tout le monde dans mon bureau!
Qu'est-ce qui se passe, Hicham?
J'étudiais les chiffres de l'agence.
Nous avons très peu de jeunes comédiens.
C'est difficile de repérer les jeunes.
La jeunesse, c'est notre avenir.
Et nous devons aussi garder nos stars.
Au fait, et Fabrice Luchini?
Il hésite à partir chez StarMedia.
J'offre une prime pour le signer.
Une prime? De combien?
Quinze mille euros pour l'agence.
Quinze mille euros? Marché conclu!
Nous allons trouver une solution immédiatement.
Let's walk through the conversation step by step.

'Everyone in my office!' Hicham gathers the whole staff for an unexpected meeting using a handy chunk meaning everybody. A nice sentence in French.

'What is going on, Hicham?' Mathias asks what is happening which is a common everyday phrase. A great expression in French.
J'étudiais les chiffres de l'agence.
'I was studying the agency figures.' Hicham explains that he spent time analyzing the numbers, using a clear cognate. You can say this in French.
Nous avons très peu de jeunes comédiens.
'We have very few young actors.' Hicham uses the descriptor meaning young to point out that the roster lacks new performers. In French, this is widely used.
C'est difficile de repérer les jeunes.
'It is hard to spot young actors.' Mathias defends the agents by explaining that scouting new talent is difficult. The French love this expression.
La jeunesse, c'est notre avenir.
'Youth is our future.' Hicham insists on this vision. He uses a word related to being young. In French, it fits perfectly.
Et nous devons aussi garder nos stars.
'And we must also keep our stars.' Andréa reminds him that established celebrities are equally essential. She uses the action meaning to keep. A nice way to say it in French.
Au fait, et Fabrice Luchini?
'By the way, what about Fabrice Luchini?' Hicham shifts the conversation using a handy phrase meaning by the way. In French, it is a great choice.
Il hésite à partir chez StarMedia.
'He is hesitating about leaving for StarMédia.' Mathias admits the actor might defect, using an action meaning to hesitate. The French find this natural.
J'offre une prime pour le signer.
'I am offering a bonus to sign him.' Built from the action meaning to offer, Hicham introduces a financial incentive. In French, this sounds very fluent.
Une prime? De combien?
'A bonus? Of how much?' Mathias immediately perks up and asks for the exact amount using a question word. The French use this structure often.
Quinze mille euros pour l'agence.
'Fifteen thousand euros for the agency.' Hicham names the generous sum on offer. In French, this phrasing is common.
Quinze mille euros? Marché conclu!
'Fifteen thousand euros? Deal!' Andréa accepts the challenge on the spot with a phrase meaning agreement concluded. You will find this useful in French.
Nous allons trouver une solution immédiatement.

'We are going to find a solution immediately.' Mathias confirms the team will take action using a clear cognate. This sounds extremely natural in French. Now listen to the whole scene again at normal speed, and see how much more you catch.

With a tempting bonus on the table, the agents suddenly unite to keep Fabrice Luchini at ASK. Listen to the scene once more to consolidate your comprehension of French business vocabulary. See you next time!
